title: Input and output table
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Selection in physical computing and Secure Your Secrets
source: Seeded from computing/y5 lesson 7 (Input and output table (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 7: A simulated micro-controller: button input, LED output. To understand how a micro-controller program links an input to an output

questions.q: Program button A to show a tick.
questions.a: on button A pressed: show icon (tick).
questions.model: Teacher drags 'on button A pressed' from Input and 'show icon' from Basic, chooses the tick, clicks A on the simulator.

questions.q: Program button B to clear the screen.
questions.a: on button B pressed: clear screen.

questions.q: What is the output in your program?
Core: Make a 'yes / no' answer box: A shows a tick, B shows a cross, A+B clears.
questions.a: on A: tick; on B: cross; on A+B: clear screen.
questions.model: Teacher builds A and B, pupils add A+B.

questions.q: Extend: Use 'show LEDs' to design your own 5 by 5 picture of a crescent moon or a star for button A.
questions.a: Any correct show LEDs pattern on button A.

questions.q: Stretch: Use 'show number' and a button to count presses. Which block stores the count?
questions.a: A variable: set count to 0; on A: change count by 1, show number count.

questions.q: An LED lighting up is... A) an input B) an output C) a condition
Name one input on a micro:bit.
questions.a: Button A, button B, light sensor or temperature sensor.
